# Best travel charger with multiple USB-C ports

**Top pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port GaN charger.** Several of the guides name it best overall.
- It has three USB-C ports and one USB-A port. One review (VoyageHacks) says all four are USB-C, so check the listing before you buy.
- Either of the first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W when used alone.
- Power splits when you plug in more devices. Two devices get 65W and 30W, and all four get 45W, 30W and 10.5W on the remaining ports.
- It is the heaviest of the group at 8.3 oz, and it comes with no cable.
- Where to buy: it's listed on Amazon through the "Check price" button in [TechWise's GaN travel charger guide](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026). I don't have a direct product URL, so confirm the port layout and price on the listing.

**Other good options**
- **Anker Prime 67W (3-port):** It is the smallest and lightest at 4.78 oz. It has two USB-C ports and one USB-A port. Either USB-C port can deliver the full 67W alone, but it drops to about 65W with two devices and 64.5W with three. It suits a laptop, a phone and one accessory. See [VoyageHacks' picks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/).
- **Anker 737 (120W):** It has two USB-C ports and one USB-A port. It is the best fit if one demanding laptop is your priority. See [TechWise's multi-device comparison](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026).
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2× USB-C + USB-A):** It costs $49.99 for a 2-pack, so you get one for home and one for your bag. It delivers 65W from either USB-C port alone and 45W plus 20W when two devices are connected. With two or more devices, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is fine for a MacBook Air but slow for a 65W laptop. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u). This is an affiliate link, and Dealectric says it had no working discount code as of Oct 24.
- **Epicka TA-105 Max (75W):** If you want plugs for other countries built in, it has three USB-C ports, two USB-A ports and swappable plugs. See [Android Central's travel adapter guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel).

**Things to know**
- Multi-port chargers share their total wattage, so plug your laptop into the strongest USB-C port first.
- The chargers above have US-style folding prongs and work on 100-240V, so abroad you only need a plug-shape adapter, not a voltage converter. Only the Epicka has international plugs built in.
- For 100W charging, use a 5A, e-marked USB-C cable. A standard cable is only rated for 60W.

**Which to pick:** Choose the UGREEN 100W if you carry a laptop, phone and tablet or watch. Choose the Anker Prime 67W if you want the lightest charger and carry only a laptop and a phone. Choose the Baseus 2-pack if you want to spend less and have a lighter laptop.
